prerequisites: It is advisable and convenient for the student to have acquired the competencies of all subjects from previous semesters, with special relevance to those corresponding to the subject "Manufacturing Engineering".

learning_outcomes.text: Ability to interpret technical documentation.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning, and to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills, and abilities in the field of Industrial Engineering.
Ability to apply knowledge in practice.
Attitude of motivation for quality and continuous improvement.

That students know how to apply their knowledge to their work or vocation in a professional way and possess the competencies that are usually demonstrated by elaborating and defending arguments and solving problems within their area of study.
That students have developed those learning skills necessary to undertake further studies with a high degree of autonomy.
Knowledge in basic and technological subjects, that enables them to learn new methods and theories, and provides them with versatility to adapt to new situations.
Ability to apply quality principles and methods.
Ability to solve problems.
Applied knowledge of manufacturing systems and processes, metrology, and quality control.
Ability to make decisions.
Ability to handle specifications, regulations, and mandatory standards.
Ability to analyze and synthesize.

Ability to draft, sign and develop projects in the field of industrial engineering whose purpose is the construction, reform, repair, conservation, demolition, manufacture, installation, assembly or operation of: structures, mechanical equipment, energy installations, electrical and electronic installations, industrial installations and plants, and manufacturing and automation processes.
Ability to direct the activities that are the object of the engineering projects described in competence G01.
Ability to analyze and assess the social and environmental impact of technical solutions.
Ability to work in a team.
Ability to work in a multidisciplinary team.
Ability to organize and plan.
Ability to apply knowledge of systems, processes, manufacturing technologies, metrology, and quality control.

syllabus_topics: Block 2. Metrology and Quality Control. 2.1. Fundamentals of Metrology. 2.2. Fits and Tolerances. 2.3. Quality Control in Manufacturing.

Block 4. Technological Fundamentals of Material Conserving Manufacturing Processes (PCCM). 4.1. Introduction to Material Conserving Forming Processes. 4.2. Casting Forming Processes. 4.3. Plastic Deformation Forming Processes.

Block 5. Technological Fundamentals of Material Adding Manufacturing Processes. Joining Technologies. 5.1. Introduction to Joining Technologies. 5.2. Technologies and Processes for Welded Joints. 5.3. Representation and Dimensioning of Welds in Drawings.
Practical Block. Practice 1. Machining. Practice 2. Machining. Practice 3. CNC Machining. Practice 4. Measurement and Verification. Practice 5. Welding. Practice 6. Welding.
Block 1. Introduction to Manufacturing Technologies. 1.1. Introduction to Manufacturing Technologies. 1.2. Annex. Mechanisms for Transmission and Transformation of Movements.

Block 3. Technological Fundamentals of Material Removal Manufacturing Processes (PCEM). 3.1. Introduction to Material Removal Forming Processes. 3.2. Non-Conventional Machining Processes. 3.3. Conventional Machining Processes. 3.4. Numerical Control Machining Processes.
teaching_methods: Theoretical classes, seminars and practical sessions using expository method/lectures, with practical application examples and possibly specialist seminars/conferences.
Practical classes/Seminars for solving exercises and problems in small work groups.
Workshop/Laboratory practical sessions in small work groups, with results incorporated into a report per student.
Individual study and autonomous work for content assimilation; group work for preparing practical reports and solving proposed problems/exercises, and possibly monographic work.
Tutorials (individual or small groups) for doubt resolution and orientation.

assessment_methods.method: Final theoretical/practical exam on course contents
Other assessable activities: Monographic work, exercises, synthesis reports, partial tests.

assessment_rules: The final theoretical/practical exam requires a minimum score of 4.5 out of 10.0 to be included in the weighted average. The Workshop/Laboratory practical questionnaire also requires a minimum score of 4.5 out of 10.0 for the weighted average. The final grade for other assessable activities will be the arithmetic mean of all submitted activities, with non-submitted activities counting as 0.0.
